AnalyticalPoint.description: Declared lengths for a trace run's analytical half; never inferred (ADR 0037).
AnalyticalPoint.title: AnalyticalPoint

Anchor.description: One hand-reviewed fact about the world. The platform spec's PerformanceRecord.
Anchor.title: Anchor

AnchorApplicability.description:
Whether one naming anchor's evidence reaches this run.

ADR 0045 retains excluded anchors with reasons; their applies is always false.

`applies` is computed over every dimension EXCEPT `STACK_VERSION` — ADR 0021's decided
item 2, option (b). Every third-party anchor differs from our stack, so counting it
would make `applies` false essentially everywhere, and a readout that is always red
carries as much information as one that is always green. The gap stays visible as a
finding; it just does not disqualify. `applies_excludes_stack_version` puts that rule in
the data rather than only in the ADR, so a UI can state it beside the verdict.
AnchorApplicability.title: AnchorApplicability

ApplicabilityDimension.description:
The nine ways an anchor's measurement can fail to reach the run in front of you.

The first eight are already fields on `Anchor`. Nothing there asks for a new anchor, a
refetch or a remeasurement — that much is a derivation over evidence the repo already
holds.

**The ninth is not an anchor's property but the run's** (ADR 0026 §4, landed by
ADR 0036 §3): `PARAMS_EDITED` says the user typed over a library parameter of the
component this anchor names, so the part measured and the part simulated are no longer
the same part. It is read from the run's `ParamOverride`s, never from a fabricated
anchor field, and ADR 0021's "may only ever weaken" validator then forces `applies`
false with no further work.
ApplicabilityDimension.title: ApplicabilityDimension

Calibration.description:
How a number came to be known. Serializes lower_snake in YAML and JSON.

There is no `spec` member — the vendor-datasheet value is `SPEC_DERIVED`.
Calibration.title: Calibration

CalibrationRef.description:
A recorded comparison of this component against an anchor. Written by P6, not by hand.

ADR 0017 §5. `rk calibrate promote` is its only writer, and every field is derivable
from the ledger entry it names. `error` is a Metric because a bare float cannot render
through <Badged>. `term` says which SplitEfficiency term the anchor supports, from the
entry's phase; it is required (non-None) exactly when the component carries a
SplitEfficiency — see `ComponentDescriptor._calibration_names_its_term`.
CalibrationRef.title: CalibrationRef

Collective.description: Names only, never costs. The cost is the fabric model's business (N0, P3).
Collective.title: Collective

ComponentApplicability.description:
One component's evidence, judged against the run that was just made.

**It may only ever weaken.** `applies_to_this_run` is false wherever `covered` is false
and is never true where `covered` is false — applicability narrows what coverage claims
and can never widen it. That is CLAUDE.md invariant 3's rule one level up, and it is a
validator rather than a convention so the bad state cannot be constructed at all.
ComponentApplicability.title: ComponentApplicability

ComponentCoverage.description:
Evidence for one component. Coverage is per component, never per system shape.

`covered` is a stored field checked against `reviewed_anchor_ids`, not a computed one:
the schema export runs in validation mode, which omits computed fields, and the UI
type would lose it.

`params_edited` narrows what `covered` may say (ADR 0026 §4, landed at the S3→S4
boundary by ADR 0036 §3). An anchor names a component by `component_id`, and a typed
parameter value keeps that id while changing the part the anchor measured — so without
this field a user edits an accelerator's bandwidth in the Builder and watches the
coverage banner stay green. It defaults to `False`, so every report written before it
existed reads exactly as it did.

**Populated by P6c (ADR 0042)** from all instances of the stored system.
P6b must still compute the ninth applicability dimension for a run.
ComponentCoverage.title: ComponentCoverage

ComponentDescriptor.description: One entry in the component library. Every param is a SourcedValue, always.
ComponentDescriptor.title: ComponentDescriptor

ComponentInstance.description:
N copies of a library component, slotted into a scope.

`fidelity` is this component's optional answer to how much the run may claim about
it; unset axes fall through to `SystemConfig.fidelity` (ADR 0011 §1). It defaults to
None, so a config written before this field existed resolves to exactly the levels it
always did.

`params` is what a user typed over the library's numbers (ADR 0026). A tuple rather
than a dict because this model is `frozen=True` and therefore hashable, and a dict
field would make `hash()` raise.
ComponentInstance.title: ComponentInstance

ComponentKind.description: The generic primitive. Adding one means a registry entry in the engine too.
ComponentKind.title: ComponentKind

ComponentRole.description: The product category. A label for humans and presets — no engine work to add one.
ComponentRole.title: ComponentRole

ComputeFidelity.description: C0 analytical · C1 contention-aware · C2 cycle-approximate · C3 external/RTL.
ComputeFidelity.title: ComputeFidelity

CoverageReport.description: `GET /calibration/coverage`. `config_hash` is None when it reports the whole library.
CoverageReport.title: CoverageReport

DimensionFinding.description:
One dimension, its verdict, and one sentence saying why.

ADR 0021 §3 sketched this as a bare 3-tuple. It is a model instead, for the reason
ADR 0017 gave for `ComponentCoverage.covered`: the UI reads it, and a tuple generates a
positional TypeScript type that nothing can read by name.
DimensionFinding.title: DimensionFinding

DimensionVerdict.description:
Three-valued, and `UNKNOWN` is never folded into `MATCHES`.

Most MLPerf rows state weight precision and no row states KV precision, so
`PRECISION_KV` is `UNKNOWN` on most anchors. A dimension the anchor is silent on is not
agreement, and a report that rounded it to agreement would claim evidence nobody has.
DimensionVerdict.title: DimensionVerdict

DurationDistribution.description: Lognormal in milliseconds: median * exp(sigma * standard_normal).
DurationDistribution.title: DurationDistribution

EpisodeCostNormalization.description:
ADR 0059: producer-owned conversion matching the selected price estimator.

Includes output from unfinished episodes; this is amortized window cost per
completion; task quality is unmodelled. Availability does not upgrade STUB.
EpisodeCostNormalization.title: EpisodeCostNormalization

EpisodeMetrics.description:
Agentic episodes: how many finished, how long they took, and where the time went.

ADR 0023; P8a populates this for agentic R1 runs. It remains `None` on chat runs.
ADR 0049 specifies mean counts across replications and completed-episode mean
shares scaled to E2E p50, then averaged across replications. These are allocations
of p50, not term percentiles; scaling and completion censoring can change the
displayed remote term even when raw per-episode waits are unchanged.
When any replication has no completed episodes, latency fields are
zero STUB placeholders with a no-samples contributor and warning, not percentiles.

**It is not a fifth metric family.** `RunResult`'s nine named fields are the metrics and
they stay nine (build-spec §2.3.3, CLAUDE.md). Everything here decomposes family 2
(latency) or counts episodes.

**Every number is a `Metric`, counts included**, because the UI renders them through
`<Badged>` and invariant 2 says numbers leave the engine badged. `seed` and `replications`
on `RunResult` are plain ints because they are *inputs*; these are outputs.

**`remote_wait_ms` is separate from `tool_cpu_ms` on purpose** (ADR 0023 §2). An agent
waiting on a remote service consumes no host CPU and no accelerator, so under contention
CPU time gets worse and remote wait does not. Folded together, a workload that is mostly
waiting looks like one that needs more cores, which is the opposite of the truth and the
exact recommendation this prototype exists to get right.

The four `*_ms` terms sum to `e2e_latency_p50_ms` within floating-point tolerance.
EpisodeMetrics.title: EpisodeMetrics

EvidenceApplicability.description:
Does the evidence behind this system reach THIS run? Rendered on Results and Compare.

Keyed on the run rather than the system: a user composing a system in the Builder has no
workload and no plan, so the question has no referent there, and `CoverageReport` stays
the right answer on that screen (ADR 0021 §1). Computed by `rk/calibration/`, never by
the engine — reading anchors is I/O and the engine is pure.
EvidenceApplicability.title: EvidenceApplicability

ExecutionPlan.description: WHERE + **HOW** + WHAT. This is the HOW.
ExecutionPlan.title: ExecutionPlan

FidelityMap.description: The C/M/N/R level a run asks for. Anything unimplemented fails loudly, by axis.
FidelityMap.title: FidelityMap

FidelityMapEntry.description:
What actually ran for one component, and how well calibrated it is.

The fidelity matrix as data — this is what the Results screen renders as its
Fidelity Map panel.

`calibration` is the WORST provenance among everything the component declares — all
of its `params`, plus its `execution_model` if it has one. It answers "how well do we
know this part", so one unsourced parameter takes the whole entry down, and a
component built entirely from datasheet numbers still reads `stub` if its efficiency
factor is a placeholder. Same worst-of rule `provenance.combine()` applies to a
Metric, applied to a component rather than to a number.

It is NOT a statement that the component's model has been validated against a
calibration anchor. That is a different axis, it needs the ledger P6 builds, and it
arrives as a separate field rather than by redefining this one — ADR 0009 §4.
FidelityMapEntry.title: FidelityMapEntry

FidelityOverride.description:
One component instance's answer to "how much may you claim about me?".

Every axis is optional: an unset axis falls through to `SystemConfig.fidelity`, which
is the run's default rather than its only answer (ADR 0011 §1). The engine has always
dispatched per component and `RunResult.fidelity_map` has always reported per
component; before this, only the *input* was system-wide, so the Fidelity Map panel
would have rendered a constant as a per-component fact.

The same `IMPLEMENTED` gate applies here as to `FidelityMap` — one rule, called twice,
never reimplemented. In practice that leaves two live choices per axis today: the
implemented level, or STUB. STUB is not a degenerate option; it is a user saying
"claim nothing about this part", which is the honest answer for a component whose
numbers we could not source.
FidelityOverride.title: FidelityOverride

LedgerEntry.description: One comparison of the simulator against one anchor.
LedgerEntry.title: LedgerEntry

Metric.description:
A number leaving the engine, with how much to trust it.

`contributors` is required and has no default: a metric that cannot name what fed
it is exactly the case `combine([])` badges STUB.

`ci95_low`/`ci95_high` stay None until the R1 DES reports replications in P5. They
exist in v0 so S4's error bars are not a schema break.
Metric.title: Metric

ModelSpec.description: MoE is active-vs-total and nothing more (build-spec §2.3.5).
ModelSpec.title: ModelSpec

NetworkFidelity.description: N0 analytical transfer · N1 flow-level · N2 packet · N3 flit/credit.
NetworkFidelity.title: NetworkFidelity

ParamOverride.description:
A value a user typed over a library parameter. ADR 0026.

**There is deliberately no `provenance` field.** A field here could spell `measured`,
and nothing downstream could then tell a typed number from the library's own. The badge
is DERIVED where the override is applied, as `combine([ESTIMATED, library.provenance])`
— worst-of, so a measured or spec-derived value becomes `estimated` and a STUB stays a
STUB, because typing over no evidence creates none.

That is CLAUDE.md invariant 3 made unrepresentable rather than merely checked: the
browser refuses to improve a badge, and so does a hand-written YAML reaching the loader
by another route.

It is NOT an exception to invariant 1. The library's claim on the world is still a
`SourcedValue` with a source and a date; this is a user's what-if about a part, and it
carries no source precisely because there is none.
ParamOverride.title: ParamOverride

Phase.description: Which half of SplitEfficiency an observation can inform. ADR 0015, P3b.
Phase.title: Phase

PowerEnvelope.description: Limits, not predictions. Violations become warnings; they never silently clamp.
PowerEnvelope.title: PowerEnvelope

Precision.description:
What the plan asks the hardware to compute in, and to store the KV cache in.

Two fields, not one: `compute` moves the compute roof and the weight bytes together,
`kv_cache` moves the memory roof's KV term on its own. ADR 0015's items 1 and 3 are
separate for exactly that reason — either alone leaves one roof precision-blind.

`compute` COVERS WEIGHTS AS WELL. A stack running fp8 GEMMs holds fp8 weights.
W8A16 — quantized weights with higher-precision compute — is NOT modelled, and is
recorded in ADR 0015 §1 as the first thing this shape would need to grow. It would be
a third field here, not a redesign.

Defaults are fp16/fp16, which is what `BYTES_PER_WEIGHT_FP16` and
`BYTES_PER_KV_ELEM_FP16` hardcoded before P3b, so an existing plan resolves to the
numbers it already produced.
Precision.title: Precision

PrecisionFormat.description:
The numeric formats a plan may ask for. ADR 0015 §1.

EXACTLY these eight. There is deliberately no FP64 member: rk-sim is an inference
simulator and nothing in scope runs fp64, so a declared fp64 peak could be loaded and
unit-checked and then never selected by any plan — a dead number in a library whose
whole point is that numbers are accountable. Decided 2026-09-13, ADR 0015 §7.6 item 2.
P3b asserts one peak-param name per member of this enum, which is what keeps the set
and the library in agreement by construction rather than by care.

`tf32` is 4 bytes. It is a 19-BIT FORMAT (1 sign + 8 exponent + 10 mantissa) held in a
32-bit slot, so its saving is in the multiplier array and not in memory. It is the one
a reader gets wrong, which is why it is called out here and in P3b's byte table.
PrecisionFormat.title: PrecisionFormat

RequestE2E.description: Arrival to last output token. R0 has no sampled percentiles (ADR 0038).
RequestE2E.title: RequestE2E

RuntimeFidelity.description: R0 ideal scheduler · R1 native-policy DES · R2 trace replay.
RuntimeFidelity.title: RuntimeFidelity

RuntimeTimeline.description:
Replication zero of one representative replica, never an averaged timeline.

Busy fractions use full bucket widths (including final padding); KV is sampled
at bucket starts, not a peak. Null pool/occupancy means unbounded, not zero.
RuntimeTimeline.title: RuntimeTimeline

RuntimeTimelineSample.description: One aligned bucket: scheduler busy fraction, start-sampled KV (ADR 0046).
RuntimeTimelineSample.title: RuntimeTimelineSample

ScalarEfficiency.description:
Realized-vs-peak as one number. The weakest value in the repo, and boxed.

build-spec §2.3.4: the platform spec says a constant efficiency factor is not good
enough in general, and it is right. We ship it anyway because per-operator kernel
efficiency needs silicon we do not have — badged ESTIMATED, named wherever a
cross-vendor comparison is shown, and sitting behind `kind` so a better model
replaces it without a schema break.
ScalarEfficiency.title: ScalarEfficiency

ScopeNode.description: A rack or a node. Scopes nest; components hang off them.
ScopeNode.title: ScopeNode

SloTargetVerdict.description:
One target the workload declared, and whether this run met it.

`metric_field` names the `RunResult` field the target was compared against, so a screen
can put the verdict beside the number it judged rather than beside a label.

**`actual` is a `Metric` and `target_ms` is a bare float, and the asymmetry is the
point** (ADR 0036 §1). `actual` is a number this engine computed — invariant 2 says it
leaves badged, the way `EpisodeMetrics` in this file already does for every one of its
terms. `target_ms` is the workload's own declaration: it defines the run and asserts
nothing about the world, which is the line invariant 1 draws for `n_layers` and ADR 0027
draws for composition counts.

`actual` IS the metric `metric_field` names — same value, unit, badge, contributors and
interval — because `run()` stamps the result's own object in after the latency badge
exists. Until it does, `_warn_about_the_slo` carries a provisional STUB-badged copy: a
missed stamp can then only ever degrade a badge, never improve one (invariant 3).
SloTargetVerdict.title: SloTargetVerdict

SloVerdict.description:
Whether the declared SLO was met — and whether the number that said so was real.

ADR 0022. The engine has always computed this; until that ADR it existed only inside a
sentence in `warnings`, which meant no sweep point could be marked infeasible, no
comparison could be sorted by feasibility, and no export could carry it. The warning is
still emitted, unchanged: it is what the Results screen's constraint banner reads.

**`certifiable` is the honest half, and it is the point of the record.** It is true only
when the number that decided the verdict is a real percentile — that is, when the run
executed at runtime R1. At R0 there is no distribution: the "p99" compared against the
target is the analytical p50 wearing a p99's name, so a met target at R0 is
`met=True, certifiable=False` and a UI must not render it as a green tick. That is
build-spec §2.4's rule — never answer a different question than the one asked without
saying so — expressed as a field instead of a paragraph.

Nothing enforces an SLO at either level. No admission control turns requests away to
protect a latency target, and `caveat` says so in the words the warning uses.

An empty verdict (`targets=()`, `met=None`) means the workload declared no SLO. It is the
default, so a run without one is not a run with an unanswered question.
SloVerdict.title: SloVerdict

SourcedValue.description:
A number entering the system, with the evidence that lets it in.

Exactly five fields. `extra="forbid"` is load-bearing: it is what rejects the
stray `note:` key that earlier drafts of the component YAML carried.
SourcedValue.title: SourcedValue

SplitEfficiency.description:
Realized-vs-peak as TWO numbers: one per roof. `kernel-efficiency.md` §5 option C.

§3 of that file established that `kernel_efficiency` is a COMPUTE-BOUND efficiency —
it multiplies the compute roof and nothing else, so for a compute-bound phase the
model's achieved-vs-peak IS that constant, while a memory-bound phase's low
achieved-vs-peak already falls out of the memory roof with nothing configured. One
scalar cannot describe both regimes.

P3's oracle measured how completely: sweeping the compute term from 1.0 to 0.1 moves
prefill 45.11 -> 451.11 ms and leaves decode BIT-IDENTICAL at 6.8726 ms at every
value, and derating bandwidth does the converse. The two axes are exactly orthogonal,
so a single term cannot reach the memory-bound phase at all (ADR 0015 §7.1).

BOTH VALUES SHIP `provenance: stub`. This member is a PLACE for evidence, not
evidence. `kernel-efficiency.md` §8's ban on fitting applies to `memory` exactly as it
applies to `compute`: nobody may put a number in either because it makes an oracle
delta smaller. And note the direction, so the temptation is visible — rk-sim's decode
is already SLOWER than GenZ, so a physically meaningful `memory` below 1 widens that
gap rather than closing it. The term is justified by physics, not by the delta's sign.
SplitEfficiency.title: SplitEfficiency

SyntheticGenerator.description: Seeded synthetic request stream. Real traces arrive as `trace_ref` in P6.
SyntheticGenerator.title: SyntheticGenerator

UpstreamRef.description:
Which pinned file, and which row of it, an anchor was copied from.

`manifest_path` is the file's `local_path` in `rk/calibration/upstream/manifest.yaml`,
which remains the single record of source, pin and licence — so no `commit_sha` here:
two vendored sources (a CI artifact, a dashboard response) have no commit to pin.
UpstreamRef.title: UpstreamRef
